value.body: Science graduates can teach in schools and colleges or work in science communication — museums, science centres, planetaria, outreach programmes, educational content and science journalism. Public bodies such as Vigyan Prasar and the National Council of Science Museums run outreach work alongside universities and research institutes.

items.label: School teaching
items.note: B.Ed is needed for most regular school teacher posts

items.label: College teaching
items.value: PG + UGC-NET / CSIR-NET / SET or Ph.D.
items.note: As per UGC regulations for Assistant Professor

items.label: Outreach employers
items.value: Science museums and centres, planetaria, research-institute outreach cells, ed-tech and media

value.title: How you get in
value.body: For schools: a B.Ed and a teacher eligibility test, then school or state recruitment. For colleges: a master's-level degree (a BS-MS counts) plus NET/SET or a Ph.D. For communication and outreach: a portfolio of writing, talks or videos; short courses help but are not mandatory.

value.title: At a glance
items: Outreach roles are fewer and often project-based or on contract.
Teaching is the larger and steadier employer, but needs the extra teaching qualification.
Many people combine research or teaching with writing and public talks.
